transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-10-22
- Start: 16:30 PDT
- Duration: ~42 minutes
- Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Jorge Ramos (CTO, Vellum), Meera Patel (ML Eng), Evan Chu (Product)

Summary: quick hands-on walkthrough of Redwood hosted Chat/Textgen API, demoing streaming behaviour, key generation params, and retry/backoff strategies. Customer emphasis on low-latency microinteractions and cost per token tradeoffs. Ask for sandbox and 48h smoke run.

Topics: streaming vs sync, temperature/top_p tradeoffs, max_tokens/response length, prefix/KV cache implications, retry/backoff patterns, idempotency, console traces, Optimize suggestions (batching/quantization).

00:00:00 Alex: hey everyone thanks for joining, I think we have about 40 minutes, uh Priya and I will run through a quick lab and then leave time for questions
00:00:12 Priya: yeah hi team, i'm Priya from Redwood infra eng, i'll drive the sandbox and show the streaming behaviour, note there may be slight caption errors in the transcript, sorry in advance
00:00:22 Jorge: sounds good, we're mostly interested in latency under 150ms P95 for short responses and how retries affect token cost, also concerned about data retention for PII
00:00:34 Alex: great that's super—thanks Jorge, that's helpful context. Meera, Evan, anything to add on constraints?
00:00:40 Meera: our current stack is a mix—some on-prem models and some hosted via another vendor, we want to compare token cost and tail latency and understand if Redwood hosted can avoid double-hops when we keep context small
00:00:54 Evan: timeline is tight, we want a POC in two weeks, but need security docs and a small smoke-run first
00:01:03 Priya: perfect, we'll show the console later; Alex will cover contract/pricing pieces. I'll start with a quick live request to the hosted Chat endpoint to show streaming differences with small tokens
00:01:15 [00:01:30] Priya: (typing) ok I'm calling the /chat/generate endpoint with a short prompt, streaming on. you'll see incremental deltas come back, and the console traces the latency per chunk
00:01:45 [00:02:05] Priya: so here the important param is 'max_tokens' and 'stop' — if you keep max_tokens low, the runtime picks a faster decoding path and KV cache warms quickly for follow ups
00:02:20 Meera: when you say KV cache warms, do you mean prefix caching across requests or per-session? we have a lot of short back-and-forths
00:02:29 Priya: good q, it's per-connection KV cache for the hosted runtime; repeated prefixes will be cached and reduce compute, but if you span multiple workers we fall back to shared disk cache policies. sometimes the transcript or docs say KV cash which is a typo we've seen in other exports
00:02:48 Jorge: interesting — how does that interact with batching? we don't want to hurt latency by aggregating short requests into large batches
00:02:57 Priya: Redwood does continuous batching with latency SLOs. you can set a max-latency window (e.g., 20ms) and the runtime will batch when it can without violating your SLO. for microinteractions you can set smaller windows or pin dedicated workers to avoid batching delays
00:03:18 [00:03:45] Alex: quick note on cost — batching typically reduces tokens-per-second cost but increases P95 depending on window. Optimize (console suggestion) will propose batching thresholds based on observed request distributions
00:03:33 Evan: and the console will show token-level cost per route?
00:03:36 Alex: yep, per-route cost and token breakdown. we'll demo after the live call
00:03:40 [00:04:00] Priya: showing retries now — i'm simulating intermittent 5xx from a worker; Redwood's client SDK has an exponential backoff with jitter, and we recommend idempotency keys for non-repeatable ops; for chat generation we suggest stateless retries with prompting to continue rather than re-sending the whole context
00:04:21 Meera: how do you handle partial streaming responses if the connection drops? do you rehydrate from the last token?
00:04:27 Priya: yes there's a resumable stream flow in the SDK — the server keeps the KV cache for a short TTL and the client can request a resume with the last acked token id. if that's not possible, fallback is to call a compatible model variant or use the last good checkpoint as prefix
00:04:45 Jorge: and how long is that TTL for KV cache?
00:04:48 Priya: default 60 seconds in hosted, configurable for Dedicated/private deployments—can be extended if you have long-running sessions
00:04:54 [00:05:20] Alex: question for the customer — what's your average prompt + response token size for these microinteractions?
00:05:25 Meera: usually the prompts are 40–80 tokens and responses 20–60 tokens, most flows are like 2–5 back-and-forths per session
00:05:33 Alex: ok that maps well to prefix caching wins and small max_tokens. you'll likely see big savings from keeping context narrow and letting the KV cache warm across the back-and-forths
00:05:42 [00:06:05] Priya: i'm switching to the Console now — you can see the live trace for the request; there's a latency waterfall and token cost per chunk. the traces also surface retries and fallback events, e.g., a fallback to smaller model family when a worker is saturated
00:06:22 [00:06:45] Priya: note on model variants — Redwood exposes curated model catalog with verified perf profiles; when capacity is constrained you can set a routing policy to prefer lower-cost quantized variants as fallback
00:06:56 Jorge: we have regulatory concerns — data residency in EU, plus SOC2 and ISO certificates; how do hosted deployments handle that?
00:07:05 Alex: hosted regions in EU are available; we have SOC2 Type II and ISO27001 documents. For stricter needs we offer Dedicated or Private with VPC peering and customer KMS/HSM. i'll attach the security pack after the call
00:07:19 Meera: do you keep logs by default? we need audit logs but must redact PII before storage
00:07:24 Alex: yes logs are retained per-route configurable; you can enable PII redaction hooks in the ingest path or use Private to keep logs in your KMS-controlled buckets. we also support configurable retention windows for audit compliance
00:07:36 [00:08:00] Priya: jumping back to params — temp and top_p control randomness, but for short deterministic replies we recommend low temperature (0.0–0.2) and top_p tuned accordingly; sometimes finite state machines + function calls give more consistent outputs than relying on low temp alone
00:08:18 Evan: can we do function/tool-calls with streaming?
00:08:22 Priya: yes, Redwood supports function calling and you can stream until function invocation, then call the function, and either stream the post-call tokens or close the stream and do a subsequent call. there are a few edge cases with idempotency we can document
00:08:35 Jorge: about cost — do you charge for tokens on retries? if the retry duplicates tokens we worry about double-billing
00:08:42 Alex: good point — Redwood charges for tokens generated by the model; retries that re-request the same generation are handled by idempotency keys on the SDK to avoid recharging for duplicate attempts when the server sees the same idempotency token. if clients re-send without idempotency then yes, it can double-charge
00:08:59 [00:09:30] Priya: live demo of a mis-ordered chunk — sometimes streaming order may change under network jitter; the SDK reassembles based on sequence ids. you might see transcribe errors in log snippets, e.g., 'temprature' instead of 'temperature' in quick notes
00:09:48 Meera: on the SDK, we plan to route through an edge proxy — any recommendations?
00:09:54 Priya: we recommend keeping the edge simple; a TCP-level proxy is fine. don't buffer streaming chunks at the proxy; that introduces latency. use health-check endpoints and circuit-breakers to let the SDK fallback to alternate regions or model variants
00:10:10 [00:10:35] Alex: talk about Dedicated vs Hosted quickly — if you need firm P95 guarantees and predictable throughput, Dedicated with reserved GPU pools is best. Hosted is faster to start and cheaper for spiky usage because of shared pools and auto-scaling
00:10:50 Jorge: ok we might want Hosted for the POC then Dedicated if we go to prod. SLA for Dedicated?
00:10:55 Alex: Dedicated SLAs include uptime guarantees and latency targets at specific commit sizes — i'll share a one-pager. also Dedicated supports extended KV cache TTLs and tighter isolation
00:11:08 [00:11:30] Priya: console Optimize tab — i'll pull up recommendation suggestions; here the system suggests a quantization profile for your workload that saves ~30% CPU/GPU with small quality delta and suggests a batching window of 12ms for current traffic shape
00:11:45 Meera: is quantization automatic? we worry about hallucination or regressions
00:11:49 Priya: Optimize proposes candidate profiles and runs quality checks against your eval set. you can opt-in progressively via a canary rollout. Redwood ties quality regressions to alerting so you can rollback quickly
00:12:08 [00:12:45] Priya: i'm going to run a quick failure-mode script; first scenario: transient 502 then retry wins — see console event: request retried with backoff, and final response delivered. second scenario: sustained worker OOM — runtime triggers model-variant fallback and emits an event
00:13:05 Evan: are those events exportable to our SIEM?
00:13:09 Alex: yes, audit logs and event streams can be shipped to your SIEM like Splunk or Datadog; Dedicated can also forward via private connectors
00:13:20 [00:13:50] Meera: for the POC we want to run 48h smoke run with our prompt set and synthetic concurrency — can you provide a sandbox and billing caps?
00:13:58 Alex: yes, we'll provision a sandbox workspace with credit limits and a captive project for your team. Priya will send the repo with the runner to replay your prompt traces
00:14:12 [00:14:40] Priya: note on idempotency patterns — for stateless chat you can attach a conversation-id and a per-turn idempotency token; the server dedups repeated identical generation requests within a short window to prevent duplicates
00:14:55 Jorge: any gotchas with streaming and mobile clients? sometimes mobile flaps cause partial streams and we have to re-request the entire response
00:15:02 Priya: mobile clients should surface partials and attempt resume with last acked token; avoid re-sending entire context from scratch. if resume isn't possible, do a lightweight reconciliation with server-side short summarization to reduce tokens
00:15:18 [00:15:40] Alex: quick recap of tradeoffs: lower max_tokens and narrower context = lower latency and cost; small batching windows = lower latency but higher cost; quantization reduces cost with potential small quality change; retries must be idempotent to avoid double charge
00:15:50 Meera: can we get an example retry policy recommended by Redwood?
00:15:54 Priya: recommended: 3 attempts, initial backoff 250ms with exponential factor 2 and randomized jitter. for long-running prompts increase initial backoff and use server-side resume. avoid aggressive immediate retries for 429s — instead honor 'Retry-After' if present
00:16:10 [00:16:30] Alex: i'll also call out the SDK telemetry we collect — latency buckets, token counts, model variant used, retries, and console traces—these help Optimize suggest settings
00:16:45 Jorge: about PII — does Redwood inspect payloads for moderation or do we need to opt-in?
00:16:50 Alex: hosted may run basic safety checks by default but PII redaction is opt-in; for enterprise you can turn off data ingestion for training/analysis. we'll include that in the security doc
00:17:06 [00:17:30] Priya: demo of the prompt set runner — i'm replaying a short script of 1000 sessions; console shows tail latency spiking under concurrent bursts, Optimize suggests widening batching window slightly to recover GPU utlization
00:17:50 Meera: would that hurt our P95 targets?
00:17:54 Priya: small tradeoff: P95 might move up 10–15ms but cost drops materially; you can use canary to weigh the change on real traffic
00:18:10 [00:18:35] Alex: next steps proposal: we'll give you 48h sandbox, Priya sends runner + quickstart, you run the smoke test with your prompt set, Redwood will review traces and propose Optimize config, then finalize pricing for Dedicated if needed
00:18:50 Evan: that works. also we need security pack and SOC2 docs before sign-off
00:18:56 Alex: yep. I'll attach both.
00:19:05 [00:19:30] Jorge: small question — do you have network egress controls for EU?
00:19:36 Alex: yes, region locking and egress rules are available, also Private supports fully air-gapped on-prem if required
00:19:44 [00:20:00] Priya: two quick implementation notes — 1) set low temperature for consistent replies, 2) use per-turn idempotency keys; we'll share code snippets.
00:20:10 Meera: on sample code, do you have examples for resumable streaming in our client stack (Node + native RN)?
00:20:18 Priya: yes, quickstart includes Node and a React Native snippet with resume handshake. we'll include it in the repo
00:20:30 [00:21:00] Alex: ok we're at about 20 minutes in, any more questions?
00:21:08 Meera: one more — how does Redwood handle model rollouts? we need predictable behavior for slight changes
00:21:15 Alex: rollouts are versioned with canary percentages and automated quality checks; you can pin a particular model version per route, or enable automatic minor updates with guardrails. Optimize runs regressions against your eval suite and can halt rollouts if quality drops
00:21:33 [00:22:00] Priya: demo of a canary — i'm switching a route to 10% new variant; console marks traffic split and shows a quick quality delta graph; if regression crosses threshold it auto-rolls back
00:22:20 Jorge: good. last item: what's the fastest we can get telemetry after a smoke run? same-day? next-day?
00:22:28 Priya: most traces are available within minutes; Optimize suggestions take a few hours to converge depending on sample size. for a 48h run you'll see robust suggestions by the end of run or next morning
00:22:42 [00:23:15] Alex: wrap-up: we'll send sandbox invite + quickstart (Priya), pricing + security pack (Alex). Customer runs 48h smoke with prompt set and sends traces to Redwood. Follow-up meeting to review results in one week, provisional slot tentatively 2026-10-29
00:23:33 Evan: confirmed tentatively 10/29, thanks
00:23:40 Jorge: thanks all, appreciated
00:23:50 Priya: thanks, we'll follow up with artifacts
00:24:00 [end of recorded portion — auto-trimmed]
